title: The brothers at the gate
hookLine: famine brings the brothers to Egypt, they don't recognize him, and he keeps his youngest brother with the cup in his bag

lines: OUT OF PRISON, OVER THE STORES.
FACES HE KNOWS IN THE LINE.
cards: A face from years ago, someone who once did real harm, a few feet away. One person knows everything. The other sees a stranger.
Yusuf is out of prison now. He asked the king to put him in charge of the storehouses, and the good years have come and gone. Now the hard years are here, just as he said.
They reach an old man and his sons in the land where Yusuf grew up. And one day, in the line of hungry travelers waiting for grain, Yusuf looks up and sees faces he'd know anywhere: his brothers.

teach.b: Surah Yusuf, verse fifty-eight: they came in to him, and he knew them, and they did not know him. In Arabic, fa-'arafahum wa-hum lahu munkirun. The whole story in a line.

The last time they saw him, he was a boy going down a well. Now he's the man who decides whether their family eats. He gives them grain generously, and even has their payment slipped back into their saddlebags.
But he asks for one thing: next time, bring your youngest brother, your father's other son. Without him, don't come back. At home, Ya'qub doesn't want to let the youngest go.
He's lost one son already on a trip with these brothers. He makes them swear to bring him back and says: Allah is the best guardian.
They return with the youngest, and Yusuf takes him aside and tells him quietly: I am your brother. Don't grieve over what they did. Then he has the king's cup placed in that brother's bag.
A herald shouts: you're thieves! The cup is found. And the brothers, under pressure, say something ugly: if he stole, well, a brother of his stole before.
They mean Yusuf, to his face, without knowing it.

teach.h: HE KEPT IT IN HIS HEART.
teach.b: The Qur'an says Yusuf kept it in his heart and did not reveal it to them. He just thought: you're in a worse place than that. Why keep his brother?

Commentators say it was a way, permitted to him, to keep the youngest safe. Some readers also see a test: would the brothers abandon another of their father's sons, as they once did? Tomorrow the story answers.

how: Muslims read Yusuf's generosity to his brothers as a model of restraint and kindness toward those who have done wrong, and Ya'qub's words, Allah is the best guardian, are often repeated when entrusting loved ones to Allah.

o: the king's vessel hidden in the youngest's bag
a drinking bowl Yusuf used in prison
a vessel of poison meant for the brothers

games.q: who did what in the story — tap the pairs.
p: knew them; they didn't know him
a brother of his stole before

s: the brothers recognized Yusuf when they came for grain
he knew them, and they did not know him.
Yusuf told his youngest brother who he was
he took him aside: I am your brother. don't grieve over what they did.
Yusuf answered the brothers' insult out loud
he kept it in his heart and did not reveal it to them.

games.q: you're Yusuf. your brothers, not knowing you, say: if he stole, a brother of his stole before. they mean you. what do you do?
o: keep it in your heart, and say nothing.
have them thrown out of Egypt.
games.why: Yusuf kept it in his heart and didn't reveal it to them. the full answer comes tomorrow.

practice: Think of someone who once wronged you, not the deepest wound, something you can hold, and picture them in front of you, not knowing everything you know.

Picture giving them something anyway, their full portion, a fair word, a favor they don't expect, not because what they did was fine, but because you'd like to be the kind of person who fills the sacks.
If you pray, you can ask for good for them.

wordCard.voice: Cup, the king's drinking vessel Yusuf hid in his young brother's bag, the test that kept him close and safe.

orig.note: Arabic, from Qur'an 12:58: "he knew them, and they did not know him."
